Thanks for the time this morning, Daniel - great conversation and really helpful context on the summarization + KPI-extraction pipeline you showed. Quick recap + next steps from our side: 

- Use case summary: ingest Q1 earnings calls and quarterly reports -> extract structured KPIs (revenue, growth %, guidance) and short bullet TL;DR for analysts. Requirement: high precision on numeric extraction, low hallucination for entity names.
- Recommended starting model(s): redwood-2-large for dev/testing, redwood-2-xl-quant (int8) for production throughput/cost tradeoff. We verified tradeoffs below.
- Redwood-verified perf (on representative FinLytics eval corpus):
  - redwood-2-large: ~120 TPS sustained, 95th latency 120ms
  - redwood-2-xl-quant (int8): ~220 TPS sustained, 95th latency 85ms
  - Note: numbers are measured with continuous batching and prefix/KV caching enabled on a Dedicated instance profile (p4d-like).

I've attached a short benchmark summary and the prompt set we used for the evals. Links are below (dashboard includes per-prompt quality slices and latency percentiles):
- Benchmark dashboard: https://app.redwood.ai/benchmarks/finlytics-20260310
- Prompt set & eval artifacts (CSV): attached 

Proposed next steps:
1) Run a quick safety/precision check on your top 50 representative docs with the prompt set we attached (takes ~1 hour of wall time).
2) If results look good, schedule a 45-minute dedicated demo with Aditya to walk through the inference profile + canary rollout plan.
3) We can pre-populate a quote and an initial canary capacity plan - will send DocuSign if you want to move forward on reserved capacity.

If you want different latency/throughput targets (e.g., prioritize <50ms p95), we can show alternate model variants + quant/compilation knobs.

Thanks - I'll follow up with Aditya to schedule the demo.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Great questions - quick answers and concrete steps: 

1) Per-prompt slices: yes - the dashboard has per-prompt precision/recall and an automatic "regression" detector that flags prompts with >5% drop vs baseline. See the "Quality slices" tab in the dashboard: https://app.redwood.ai/benchmarks/finlytics-20260310 (we highlighted the top 10 failure prompts).

2) Hallucination / temperature: our evals used deterministic decoding for extraction prompts (greedy) when extracting numeric/entity fields. For generative TL;DRs we used top-p 0.9 with temperature 0.6 and a length penalty tuned for short outputs. For extraction-heavy flows, we recommend: 
   - decoding: greedy or beam width 3 for critical fields
   - safety: run an NER-based post-check for entities + numeric range assertions
   - prompt-engineering: explicit field tags and examples (see attached prompt CSV)

3) Dedicated test pool lead time: we can spin up a small Dedicated pool (2-4 GPUs equivalent) in 5 business days after PO. If procurement needs an SOX/SLA question answered, loop in procurement@finlytics.com and we'll get docs.

I've added: 
- Demo booking link (Aditya): https://cal.com/aditya-redwood/demo (suggest Tues 3/16 or Wed 3/17 after 11am ET)
- Pre-filled quote / DocuSign: https://docusign.com/tx/XYZ123
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DEAL-7890

Would you like us to run the 50-doc sample on our Dedicated test pool and share the slice report, or do you prefer to run it on your side first? If you want us to run it, we'll need sample docs and a short NDA (if data is sensitive).

Thanks - looping Aditya to coordinate the demo and the quick eval run.

Best,
Marissa
